name: Juan Perón
summary: Perón built Justicialism around organized labor, social rights, state-directed industrial development and national economic independence. His governments expanded political participation through women’s suffrage while concentrating executive power and restricting opposition media. Abroad he advocated a Third Position between the major power blocs.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Article 37 of the 1949 constitution made pay sufficient for workers' vital needs part of the right to fair remuneration.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Perón's 1949 reform entrusted foreign trade to the state and authorized intervention in production and distribution when required for the general interest.

public-ownership.rationale: Article 40 made public utilities and major energy resources public property and required the transfer of privately held utilities to public ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Under Perón the 1973 tax reform replaced fixed corporate assessments with progressive personal taxes on shareholders and adopted progressive taxes on most forms of property.

unions-good.rationale: The 1949 constitution recognized worker organization and collective defense of occupational interests as basic worker rights.

property-fundamental.rationale: Article 38 subjected ownership to obligations for the common good and let Congress authorize compensated expropriation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Article 40 prohibited enterprises from dominating markets, eliminating competition or extracting usurious profits, and authorized public economic intervention.

strong-leader.rationale: Perón used the impeachment and replacement of most Supreme Court justices to consolidate executive authority.

state-harmful.rationale: Perón drove a constitutional reform that expanded the state's responsibilities for the economy and social welfare.

decide-locally.rationale: In El gobierno, Perón assigns direction to central government while putting implementation at decentralized levels.

traditional-family.rationale: In El hombre, la familia, la sociedad y la cultura, Perón treats marriage as the basis of a durable family and the family as the basic social unit.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Article 37 placed Argentina's artistic and historical heritage under state protection.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Article 17 instructed the federal government to encourage immigration and barred entry restrictions on foreigners coming to farm, teach or develop industry.

free-trade.rationale: Article 40 reserved imports and exports to the state under conditions set by legislation.

limit-growth.rationale: Perón called for limits on resource-intensive growth in highly industrialized economies and for production to be redirected toward essential needs with lower resource use.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Perón warned against overestimating technology and argued that technical advances could not substitute for the natural processes on which people depend.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Perón approved the Embalse nuclear plant construction agreement through Decree 706/74, and Atucha I began supplying the national grid during his presidency.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Article 3 of Perón's 1973 industrial promotion law retained ordinary import duties on capital goods with suitable domestic equivalents while allowing reductions where local supply was inadequate.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Perón's 1973 industrial promotion law earmarked public development finance for industrial priorities, building on the state economic powers established in 1949.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The financial reform under Perón gave the central bank the power to determine the money supply and imposed controls on private-bank lending.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Law 14,250 made ministry-approved collective agreements binding across the covered trade, including on employers and workers who did not sign them.

direct-votes.rationale: The 1949 reform vested national legislative power in Congress and Article 14 reserved government and deliberation to the people's representatives and constitutional authorities.

workers-councils.rationale: Perón's constitutional reform vested national legislative power in a Congress with a Chamber of Deputies and a Senate.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Writing in exile about the outlawing of Justicialism, Perón defended resistance outside the law when the authorities had closed electoral and peaceful avenues.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1949 reform retained public support for Roman Catholicism and required the president and vice-president to be Catholic.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Articles 91–96 gave federal judicial authority to a public Supreme Court and lower public courts.

self-interest-moral.rationale: In El modelo argentino, Perón argues that the economy must serve social purposes and that a social ethic must supersede individualism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Perón's fifteenth truth treats individual rights and community rights as claims to be balanced, giving neither categorical precedence.

limit-population.rationale: Perón called for immediate planning to slow unsustainable population growth, with methods tailored to national conditions and an explicit exception for Argentina.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Perón's government pursued industrial development as a principal objective of its 1973 economic program.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Perón argued that technological change was outpacing society's ability to adapt and called for limits where it damaged ecological and social conditions.

restore-past-order.rationale: In El hombre, la familia, la sociedad y la cultura, Perón rejects simply repeating the past and calls for carrying durable values into future development.

production-for-use.rationale: Perón calls for ending profit and waste as the basic motives of production and prioritizing essential human needs.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: In El modelo argentino, Perón proposes political pluralism with representation for the full range of organized social groups and rejects a single-party system.

collective-farming.rationale: Article 38 directed the state to help farming families acquire ownership of the land they worked.

taxation-theft.rationale: The reform retained congressional taxation as a source of public revenue and specified equity and proportionality as the basis of taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Article 30 protected private conduct from state intervention only if it also respected public order and morals.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Article 37 expressly recognized rights of the family as a social unit.

conscription.rationale: Article 32 obliged citizens to bear arms in defense of Argentina and its constitution as provided by law.

organic-representation.rationale: The 1949 constitution retained an elected legislature constituted by territorial constituencies and did not transfer its role to organized occupational groups.

universal-morality.rationale: In El hombre, la familia, la sociedad y la cultura, Perón calls for a social ethic grounded in permanent principles that people share across societies.

single-common-good.rationale: Perón's first truth says government should serve a single interest, that of the people.

class-collaboration.rationale: Perón maintained the 1973 Social Pact, which brought employers and organized labor together under government coordination on wages, prices and incomes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Article 37 put cultural treasures under public protection and authorized expropriation to safeguard them.

dominated-front.rationale: Perón calls for solidarity among Third World countries in defending their resources against international monopolies based in highly industrialized economies.

ban-interest.rationale: Article 37 recognized interest on capital as a form of return, while Article 40 distinguished ordinary returns from usurious profits.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Perón's 1949 constitution expressly disallowed racial distinctions in law and placed all inhabitants on an equal legal footing.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The reform imposed wide public responsibilities for health, education, social security and the economy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Article 28 made all inhabitants equal before the law and rejected privileges of blood or birth.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Perón maintained and gave statutory force to religious instruction in state schools early in his presidency. In 1955 he promulgated Law 14,401 repealing the religious instruction law.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Article 15 withheld state recognition from organizations hostile to the freedoms guaranteed by the constitution or to democratic government.

separated-powers.rationale: Perón's constitutional reform maintained separate branches and judicial tenure. He also consolidated executive power by impeaching and replacing most Supreme Court justices.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Perón treats hunger as an immediate problem of production and distribution and gives improving both priority over demographic planning.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The 1949 constitution put the presidency and both chambers of Congress to election by the people.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Article 34 allowed the suspension of guarantees in emergencies. After the 1951 military uprising, Perón's government used internal-war powers to hold opponents indefinitely.

party-controls-media.rationale: Perón's government expropriated the opposition newspaper La Prensa and transferred it to the allied labor federation.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Article 31 allowed foreigners to naturalize after two years of residence and provided for automatic acquisition of nationality after five years, subject to its conditions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Article 83 made the president commander in chief of all armed forces.

clerical-rule.rationale: Perón's reform reserved the presidency and legislative authority to elected officials in a representative republic.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Perón drove the reform whose Article 78 allowed presidential reelection without a numerical limit, and he ran again under it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Perón moved to secure ratification of the inter-American mutual defense treaty in 1950, committing Argentina to a standing defense arrangement.

people-in-arms.rationale: In Las Fuerzas Armadas, Perón identifies the professional armed forces as the backbone of Argentine national defense.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: In El ámbito económico, Perón ties the country's ability to make sovereign decisions to control of its productive resources and development.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Perón drove a constitutional revision implemented through a separately elected constituent convention in 1949.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Article 82 replaced the electoral college for president and vice-president with direct popular election.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article 38 gave private property a social function and subjected it to obligations established by law for the common good.

collective-defense.rationale: Perón worked to secure Argentine ratification of the Rio Treaty, which treats an armed attack on one American signatory as an attack on all.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Perón combined the presidency with control of the governing party and used that position to consolidate political power.

ban-cartels.rationale: Article 40 prohibited arrangements aimed at dominating domestic markets, eliminating competition or making usurious profits.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Article 28 expressly barred titles of nobility and privileges based on blood or birth.

patriotic-education.rationale: Article 37 charged education with cultivating civic virtues and required university instruction on Argentina and its historical mission.

delink-world-market.rationale: In El ámbito de la política exterior, Perón calls for intensifying economic relations with all countries regardless of ideology.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Articles 21 and 35 protected constitutional rights against ordinary legislation and required a special amendment process.

elective-rulers.rationale: Article 82 put the federal presidency to direct popular election.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Article 22 made the constitution supreme and required national laws to conform to it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: In El hombre, la familia, la sociedad y la cultura, Perón asks citizens to participate actively in public life and take responsibility for the community.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Perón argues that affluent industrial economies sustain wasteful consumption by drawing heavily on resources extracted from the Third World.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: In El ámbito económico, Perón treats domestic effort as the basis of development and foreign capital as a supplementary resource.

filial-duty.rationale: Article 37 made care for older people a family responsibility and allowed public authorities to claim contributions from relatives who failed to support them.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Article 68 gave Congress authority to set the national administration's expenditure budget and approve or reject its accounts.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Perón urged societies to replace superfluous consumption with education and healthy leisure and argued that wasteful affluent consumption harms human well-being.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: In El ámbito de la política exterior, Perón makes state sovereignty and the self-determination of peoples conditions of international cooperation.

corporate-influence.rationale: In El ámbito político, Perón argues that groups linked to economic power infiltrate parties and pressure government decisions.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: In El ámbito de la política exterior, Perón makes respect for state sovereignty, self-determination and ideological pluralism basic rules of Argentine foreign policy.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Article 37 required the state to protect marriage and guarantee spouses' legal equality.

informal-organisation.rationale: In La comunidad organizada, Perón calls for stable organization across society as protection against tyranny.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Article 19 required treaties to conform to the principles of public law established in the constitution.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Perón's Third Position calls for smaller states to keep their political independence between the rival great-power blocs.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Perón's Law 13,047 set a framework for subsidizing qualifying private schools that provided officially recognized education.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: In El modelo argentino, Perón formulates Justicialism as a third position rejecting both capitalist individualism and communist collectivism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Perón's government expropriated the opposition newspaper La Prensa and used internal-war powers to detain political opponents after the 1951 uprising.

participatory-democracy.rationale: In La comunidad organizada, Perón calls for citizens to participate through social organizations as well as political parties.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Article 36 grounds constitutional rights in popular sovereignty, while the preamble invokes God as a source of reason and justice.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: In Las Fuerzas Armadas, Perón makes the armed forces integral to national defense.

rich-first.rationale: Perón's 1973 industrial promotion law directed stronger incentives toward lagging regions and restricted further industrial concentration around Buenos Aires.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Perón secured ratification of the Rio Treaty, placing Argentina in the United States-led inter-American mutual defense system during the Cold War.

racial-franchise.rationale: The 1949 constitution rejected racial distinctions and provided for direct popular election without an ethnic qualification.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: In El ámbito económico and El ámbito político, Perón ties concentration of income to social conflict and organized economic power to pressure on democratic decisions.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Perón's administration initially maintained Catholic instruction in public schools. Its later abolition withdrew religious instruction without establishing atheist instruction.

term-limits.rationale: Perón's reform allowed unlimited reelection for the presidency and for members of both chambers of Congress.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Perón called rapid collective action against ecological destruction a first priority and described the current course as a threat to humanity's survival.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Article 37 explicitly committed the state to legal equality between spouses.

abolish-ip.rationale: Article 38 protected authors' and inventors' exclusive rights for the period prescribed by law.

independent-unions.rationale: Perón used official union recognition and government intervention in unions to subordinate independent labor leadership.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Article 40 established public ownership of public services and required their transfer from private owners by purchase or expropriation.

second-chamber.rationale: Article 41 vested legislative power in a Congress with a Chamber of Deputies and a Senate.

family-wage.rationale: Article 37 defined worker welfare in relation to a livelihood sufficient for the worker and the worker's family.

spiritual-nature.rationale: In El hombre, la familia, la sociedad y la cultura, Perón includes the highest interests of the human spirit among the community's obligations.

communal-electorates.rationale: The 1949 constitution elected deputies and senators through territorial constituencies rather than distinct religious constituencies.

free-public-college.rationale: Perón's Decree 29,337 suspended public university tuition and provided for government funding to compensate the institutions.

future-generations.rationale: In La política ecológica, Perón describes preserving natural resources and the environment as a duty of current generations to later ones.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Law 14,250 gave state-approved agreements negotiated by unions and employers legal force for the trade.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Perón calls for changing how the global economy uses Third World resources and prioritizing the basic needs and industrial development of poorer countries.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: In El modelo argentino, Perón's social democracy requires participation through organized sectors and a social purpose extending beyond electoral procedure.

women-suffrage.rationale: Perón promulgated Law 13,010, which gave women the same political rights and electoral obligations as men.

indirect-election.rationale: Perón's reform made election to the presidency and both houses of Congress direct.

national-church-status.rationale: Article 2 singled out the Catholic Church for federal support, and Article 77 required the head of state to be Catholic.

simple-living.rationale: Perón calls for giving up some material comforts and replacing superfluous goods with education and healthy recreation.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: In El ámbito político, Perón gives parties the primary role in political representation and gives social organizations a further representative role.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Article 31 of the 1954 divorce reform let either spouse petition for full dissolution of the marriage a year after a legal separation judgment.

national-resource-control.rationale: Article 40 vested minerals, oil, gas and other natural energy resources in the nation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Perón advocated organizing an independent Third World alongside the two dominant blocs.

no-central-bank.rationale: The financial reform during Perón's last administration expanded the central bank's control over credit and the money supply.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: In El ámbito económico, Perón rejects increasing capital's remuneration at labor's expense as socially unjust.

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: Perón's constitutional reform assigned federal trials to courts and dropped the earlier constitution's explicit jury-trial provision.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: Article 40 placed natural energy resources in national ownership while providing for provincial shares of their proceeds.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: Perón pursued industrial expansion as a way to restore and develop Argentina's productive economy.

pay-for-effort.rationale: Article 37 made both the work accomplished and the effort expended criteria for fair pay.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Article 3 of Perón's industrial promotion law let companies apply certain investment certificates toward an income-tax liability, maintaining the tax as part of the promotion program.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: Perón maintained the Social Pact's price freeze as a central instrument of anti-inflation policy in 1973–74.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: Perón explicitly defended the resort to clandestine resistance by a banned movement after it had been denied legal and electoral means to act.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Article 38 called for the state to help farming families own the soil they worked.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Perón's reform vested economic direction in the state while Law 14,250 gave recognized unions a specific bargaining role alongside employers.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Article 37 made fair remuneration and proper working conditions basic rights within wage employment.

civil-marriage.rationale: Perón's 1954 reform altered the civil marriage regime to let spouses dissolve a civil marriage and marry again.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Article 37 recognized worker welfare, social security, adequate housing and protection for older people as matters of public responsibility.

notes: Reviewed economy, government, society, foreign policy, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, methods of change and global integration. The 1949 constitutional reform is used where Perón drove the change. The foreign-policy evidence distinguishes his Third Position from his government’s actual ratification of the inter-American defense treaty. Later enactments under Isabel Perón were excluded. The 1972 environment message and chapters of the 1974 Modelo on technology and ecology document period-specific positions, while most present-day technology questions remain unanswered.
